title: Archive a timestamped operator price snapshot every week
problem: Every CLV and 'market vs model' statement currently rests on an aggregator line whose timestamp is unknown (F01). Without a price history, gate G4 can never be evaluated and no strategy can be certified as skill.
recommendation: Capture the operator's own NFL page (spread, total, moneyline) at two fixed times per week (Wednesday post-injury-report and Sunday pre-kickoff) and store the raw snapshot with HTTP headers and hash.
review_test: If the operator page blocks automated capture or terms forbid it, fall back to manual capture of 5 games per week and mark the sample as partial.

title: Ship a sign-convention regression test with every backtest
problem: This session's first injury backtest reported a 57.4% ATS edge that vanished once the spread sign convention was corrected (nflverse spread_line is the expected home margin, not a handicap). A single sign error is enough to invent an edge.
recommendation: Add a unit test that asserts the ATS sign on a synthetic fixture, plus a known-answer test on 10 historical games with published results, and fail the build if either drifts.
evidence: verification.html#sign; data/decision-desk/claim_checks.csv row 'Injury-driven lineup loss is not priced by the market'
review_test: If a future data feed documents a different convention, update the fixture rather than the assertion, and record the change.

title: Pre-register the variant count before looking at results
problem: Bonferroni only means something if the number of tested variants is honest. Buckets like 'gap >= 50 pp' were found after inspection, which inflates the true false-discovery rate.
recommendation: Write the strategy list and thresholds into research/38a1fc27/strategies.md, commit it, and require the commit hash in the results table. Count every variant, including abandoned ones.
review_test: If a strategy must be added after the fact, it starts in a new pre-registration round with its own alpha budget.

title: Publish a market-efficiency scorecard per signal
problem: We can measure whether a signal predicts results, but the useful question is whether the market has already priced it. Injury deficiency moves the line (-0.021 pts per pp) but its ATS residual edge is 51.4% with p=1.0.
recommendation: For each signal, report (a) regression of the market line on the signal, (b) regression of the ATS residual on the signal, (c) the implied 'priced share'. Rank ideas by residual edge, not by raw predictive power.
review_test: If a signal shows residual edge with a verified closing price, promote it to a full gate evaluation.

title: Use lineup deficiency as a pricing input for our own lines, not as a bet trigger
problem: The measured relationship is real for predicting margin (about -0.039 points per percentage point of relative deficiency, p=6e-5), but the market already moves about half of it and the residual ATS record is 51.4% (p=1.0).
recommendation: Feed deficiency into the line model (already implemented) and stop advertising it as a betting signal. Show the model line both with and without the adjustment so the size of the adjustment is auditable.
review_test: If a future season shows a residual edge with verified prices, revisit.

title: Extend depth tracking to offensive-line continuity
problem: Offensive line injuries are the classic source of hidden lineup decay: five players who never practised together still count as 'starters available'. Snap share alone cannot see that.
recommendation: Build a weekly starting-five continuity metric (same five linemen starting together, consecutive weeks) from snap counts and measure its relationship to sacks allowed, pressure rate and ATS residual.
evidence: injuries.html#methodology; snap counts pinned in data/decision-desk/raw
review_test: If continuity shows no relationship to pressure or margin after a season of data, drop it.

title: Treat practice-status transitions as a probability, not a label
problem: The official report gives three practice levels and a game status. Collapsing them to fixed weights (A1/A2) throws away the strongest information: a player moving DNP -> LP -> FP across the week.
recommendation: Fit the mapping empirically: P(active) by (practice sequence, game status) from 2023-2026 reports, and publish the fitted table with sample sizes.
review_test: If the fitted probabilities differ from the assumed weights by less than 5 percentage points, keep the simple weights.

title: Score the leaderboard on CLV and calibration, never on win rate
problem: A win-rate leaderboard rewards luck and variance; over 300 bets a 52% and a 56% record are statistically indistinguishable.
recommendation: Rank by de-vigged CLV first, calibration second, flat-stake yield third; require a 300-bet minimum and publish confidence intervals next to every rank.
review_test: If CLV data cannot be captured (S01 fails), the board stays provisional and unranked.

title: Make the data layer dual-source with automatic disagreement alerts
problem: The pipeline depends on one aggregator mirror. If it drifts from the official page, every downstream number drifts silently.
recommendation: Every build already fetches the official page and the mirror; add a hard assertion that the two agree row-for-row on the injury report and standings (currently 276/276 and 32/32), and fail the build on any mismatch.
review_test: If the official page layout changes and parsing fails, fail closed (blank + flag) rather than falling back silently.

title: Model opponent-adjusted efficiency, not raw points
problem: The current ratings use final margins with a two-way fit; they cannot distinguish a good offence beating bad defences from a mediocre one.
recommendation: Add EPA per play (offence and defence) from the same pinned source, blend with the margin model, and evaluate whether it reduces out-of-sample log-loss.
review_test: Promote when play-by-play ingestion is in place and the blend beats the margin model on holdout log-loss.

title: Price correlated legs with an empirical copula, and refuse independent pricing
problem: Same-team QB + WR1 legs are correlated (r = 0.50 on 2024-2026); at median lines the joint hit rate is 32.5% versus 24.8% if treated as independent, a +7.7 pp gap that changes the fair price materially.
recommendation: Require an empirical joint estimate for any same-game combination; publish the implied fair price next to the offered price and reject the bet when the offered price assumes independence.
review_test: If the operator's SGP price already reflects the correlation (compare implied joint to empirical), no action is needed beyond documentation.

title: Keep a decision log (one line per accepted suggestion)
problem: Suggestions accepted without a recorded rationale get re-litigated, and rejected ones get re-proposed.
recommendation: Append an ADR row when a suggestion moves to Accepted/Rejected: date, decision, evidence, owner, revisit date.
review_test: If the log has fewer than one entry per accepted suggestion, the process is not being followed.

title: Separate OFFICIAL and AGGREGATOR tiers in every table, mechanically
problem: Mixing an official injury row and a mirror-derived snap profile in one 'verified' column invites over-claiming.
recommendation: Every table carries a tier column; a build check fails if an OFFICIAL-labelled row's source URL is not on an official domain.
review_test: If a needed dataset has no official publisher, label it AGGREGATOR and keep the claim language narrow.

title: Cap and retire strategies on a schedule, not on a hunch
problem: Unlimited strategy proliferation guarantees a false discovery; the more families tested, the higher the alpha needed.
recommendation: Budget one new family per week, retire any family that fails gates for two consecutive seasons, and publish the retirement list.
review_test: If the family budget blocks a genuinely new mechanism, allow an exception with a doubled alpha requirement.

title: Add a weather and venue adjustment to the total model
problem: The totals model ignores wind, temperature and roof; domes and high-wind games are systematically mis-totalled.
recommendation: Join official game-time weather and roof data, fit a wind/temperature adjustment on historical totals, and show the adjusted total beside the raw one.
review_test: Promote if more than 80% of games have non-null weather in the pinned source.

title: Publish the reward structure only after the jurisdiction question is closed
problem: The brief asks for rewards for top-performing strategies, but cash prizes raise licensing, tax and eligibility questions that no public source answers for this project.
recommendation: Run the competition as points-only until Q04/Q05 are answered; publish the intended cash structure as a proposal, not a commitment.
review_test: Close Q04/Q05 first; then publish reward terms with eligibility rules.
